################################################################################ 

# 0. OVERVIEW & SETUP

################################################################################ 

This script presents main analyses, including correlations, descriptive
visualisations, two-stage meta-analyses, and multi-level models for
moderation tests.

For sex disaggregation analyses, see 'Sex disaggregated.Rmd'.

For sensitivity analyses, see

- 'Sensitivity analysis - Meta-regressions.Rmd' for meta-regressions

- 'Sensitivity analysis - Excluding no denomination.Rmd' for repeat of
  all analyses excluding no denomination group

- 'Sensitivity analysis - Largest group.Rmd' for repeat of all analyses
  with the largest group as majority (rather than \>50%)

### **Setup**

Load functions, file paths, and packages

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE)

# Set cran repo
options(repos = c(
  CRAN      = "https://cloud.r-project.org",
  CRANextra = "https://cloud.r-project.org"
))


# Load packages (and update if necessary)
if (!require("pacman")) install.packages("pacman")
pacman::p_load(
  # Data wrangling
  tidyverse, dplyr, broom,
  # Models
  lme4, lmerTest, emmeans, metafor, broom.mixed, purrr,
  # Visualisations
  visdat, ggplot2, flextable, officer, sf, countrycode, rnaturalearth, grid, scales, forestploter, ggrepel, patchwork
)

# Read in cleaned dataset
data <- readRDS("data.rds")

# Check data
data %>% colnames()
data %>% nrow() # n = 95,366 - correct
```

Define function for making demographic table

```{r}
make_table <- function(df, country_sample_sizes) {
  
  country_religion_composition <- df %>%
    filter(!is.na(religion_status)) %>%
    group_by(country) %>%
    mutate(country_n = n()) %>%
    group_by(country, religion_wrd, religion_status) %>%
    summarise(
      n = n(),
      country_n = first(country_n),
      .groups = "drop_last"
    ) %>%
    mutate(pct_of_country = n / country_n * 100) %>%
    ungroup()
  
  majority_table <- country_religion_composition %>%
    filter(religion_status == "Majority") %>%
    select(
      country,
      majority_religion = religion_wrd,
      majority_pct = pct_of_country
    )
  
  minority_summary <- country_religion_composition %>%
    filter(religion_status == "Minority") %>%
    arrange(country, desc(pct_of_country)) %>%
    group_by(country) %>%
    summarise(
      minority_composition = paste0(
        religion_wrd, " (", round(pct_of_country, 1), "%)",
        collapse = "; "
      ),
      minority_pct_total = round(sum(pct_of_country), 1),
      .groups = "drop"
    )
  
  table <- country_sample_sizes %>%
    left_join(majority_table, by = "country") %>%
    left_join(minority_summary, by = "country")

  return(table)
}
```

# 1. CHECK & TRANSFORM DATA

## Categorise majority/minority

In primary analysis, we operationalise majority as a the religious group
with \>=50% of the population share. In 'Sensitivity analysis - Largest
group' we will change the operationalisation to majority being the
largest religious group.

We have data on the religious demographics of each country, as well as
the religious affiliation of each respondent. We can use this to
categorise whether each respondent is part of the religious majority or
minority in respective countries.

We have to **drop countries that do not have a majority group** in
primary analysis.

```{r categorise-maj-min}

## ---- Create religion majority/minority status variable ----

# Group all religious demographic stats together 
religion_pct_vars <- c(
  "buddhist_pct",
  "chinese_folk_religionist_pct",
  "christian_pct",
  "confucianist_pct",
  "daoist_pct",
  "ethnic_religionist_pct",
  "hindu_pct",
  "jain_pct",
  "jew_pct",
  "muslim_pct",
  "shintoist_pct",
  "sikh_pct",
  "spiritist_pct",
  "other_religion_pct",
  "no_denomination_pct" 
)

## ---- Match religion label to WRD % ----
# Labels have to match religion_wrd / majority_religion values
religion_pct_map <- tibble(
  religion = c("Buddhist", "Chinese_folk_religionist", "Christian", "Confucianist",
               "Daoist", "Ethnic_religionist", "Hindu", "Jain", "Jew", "Muslim",
               "Shintoist", "Sikh", "Spiritist", "Other", "No_Denomination"),
  pct_var  = religion_pct_vars
)

wrd_long <- data %>%
  distinct(country, across(all_of(religion_pct_vars))) %>%
  pivot_longer(all_of(religion_pct_vars),
               names_to = "pct_var", values_to = "wrd_share") %>%
  left_join(religion_pct_map, by = "pct_var") %>%
  select(country, religion, wrd_share)

# Checks 
wrd_long %>% count(country, religion) %>% filter(n > 1) # none
setdiff(unique(data$religion_wrd), religion_pct_map$religion) # none

## ---- Identify countries with no majority ----

countries_no_majority <- data %>%
  distinct(country, across(all_of(religion_pct_vars))) %>%
  rowwise() %>%
  mutate(
    max_pct = max(c_across(all_of(religion_pct_vars)), na.rm = TRUE)
  ) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  filter(max_pct <= 50) %>%
  pull(country) %>%
  unique()

countries_no_majority 
# China, Hong Kong, South Korea, Nigeria, Singapore, Taiwan, Vietnam


## ---- Categorise majority vs minority for countries ----

data <- data %>%
  mutate(
    majority_religion = case_when(
      christian_pct > 50 ~ "Christian",
      muslim_pct > 50 ~ "Muslim",
      hindu_pct > 50 ~ "Hindu",
      buddhist_pct > 50 ~ "Buddhist",
      jew_pct > 50 ~ "Jew",
      no_denomination_pct > 50 ~ "No_Denomination",
      daoist_pct > 50 ~ "Daoist",
      confucianist_pct > 50 ~ "Confucianist",
      ethnic_religionist_pct > 50 ~ "Ethnic_religionist",
      shintoist_pct > 50 ~ "Shintoist",
      sikh_pct > 50 ~ "Sikh",
      spiritist_pct > 50 ~ "Spiritist",
      jain_pct > 50 ~ "Jain",
      chinese_folk_religionist_pct > 50 ~ "Chinese_folk_religionist",
      other_religion_pct > 50 ~ "Other",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    )
  )


## ---- Categorise majority vs minority for individuals ----
# Majority group as >50%

data <- data %>%
  mutate(
    religion_status = case_when(
      is.na(religion_wrd) ~ NA_character_,
      religion_wrd == majority_religion ~ "Majority",
      TRUE ~ "Minority"
    )
  )

```

We have categorised individuals as being part of majority or minority
religious now!

Now, we do spot checks to check that all religions are covered in the
sample, and that all respondents have been categorised as a religious
majority or minority. All individuals missing on religious affiliation
have been removed so everyone should be mapped.

Other than removing countries with no majority group, we also have to
**drop countries if the majority group is not present in the WVS
sampl**e.

```{r check-categorisations}

## ---- Sanity & spot checks ----

# Check everyone is mapped
data %>% count(religion_wrd, useNA = "ifany") # All religions covered in the sample (inc others)

data %>% count(religion_status, useNA = "ifany") # All respondents are mapped as majority or minority

# Spot checks
data %>% filter(country == "India") %>% count(religion_wrd, religion_status)
data %>% filter(country == "Macao SAR China") %>% count(religion_wrd, religion_status)

## Interestingly, in Macao SAR China, although Chinese folk-religonists are technically the majority, none are recruited in WVS sample. This is likely because WVS does not include chinese folk religionists as a broad category, only Buddhists/ no denomination. 
## We will drop Macao in the analyses as there is no comparison to a majority.

# Check number of countries
data$country %>% n_distinct() 


## ---- Check composition of majority and minority groups for all countries in WVS sample ----
country_religion_composition <- data %>%
  filter(!is.na(religion_status)) %>%
  group_by(country) %>%
  mutate(country_n = n()) %>%
  group_by(country, religion_wrd, religion_status) %>%
  summarise(
    n = n(),
    country_n = first(country_n),
    .groups = "drop_last"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    pct_of_country = n / country_n * 100
  ) %>%
  ungroup() 
# country_religion_composition %>% view()
```

Interestingly in Macao, although Chinese folk-religionists are
technically the majority, none are recruited in the sample - likely
because WVS does not include Chinese folk religionists as a broad
category, only a smaller 'other' category; only Buddhists or no
denomination are broad categories. We cannot however collapse Chinese
folk religionists into Buddhists due to the tangible distinction in
World Religion Database. Macao is thus dropped from analyses because
there is no comparison to a majority.

We now have 57 countries remaining.

Next, we drop **countries with minorities that are \<1% of the WVS
sample.** Sample sizes would be too small to be compared meaningfully to
the majority.

```{r check-small-minorities}
# Check with countries have <1% minority group ----
country_check <- data %>%
  group_by(country) %>%
  summarise(
    n_total = n(),
    n_majority = sum(religion_status == "Majority", na.rm = TRUE),
    n_minority = sum(religion_status == "Minority", na.rm = TRUE),
    pct_majority = 100 * n_majority / n_total,
    pct_minority = 100 * n_minority / n_total,
    n_groups = n_distinct(religion_status),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  arrange(pct_minority)
country_check %>% print(n=57)
# All countries have both majorities and minorities. 3 countries have minority <1%.
```

We have now filtered countries that 1) do not have a religious majority
(\>=50%), 2) majority/minority not present in the WVS sample, and 3)
minority is \<1% of the WVS sample.

There are 54 countries remaining in the dataset.

# 2. DEMOGRAPHICS TABLE

First, we create a demographic table of countries that were excluded.

```{r demographics-excluded-from-main}
# Demographics table for all countries that were excluded from main analyses
countries_to_show <- c(
  "China", "Hong Kong SAR China", "South Korea", "Nigeria", "Singapore",
  "Taiwan", "Vietnam", "Macao SAR China", "Libya", "Iraq", "Maldives"
)

# Check names match before proceeding
setdiff(countries_to_show, unique(data$country))

data_subset <- data %>% filter(country %in% countries_to_show)

country_sample_sizes <- data_subset %>%
  group_by(country) %>%
  summarise(sample_size = n()) %>%
  arrange(country)

table_subset <- make_table(
  df = data_subset,
  country_sample_sizes = country_sample_sizes
)

majority_minority_n <- data_subset %>%
  filter(!is.na(religion_status)) %>%
  group_by(country, religion_status) %>%
  summarise(n = n(), .groups = "drop") %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = religion_status, values_from = n) %>%
  rename(majority_n = Majority, minority_n = Minority)

table_subset <- table_subset %>%
  left_join(majority_minority_n, by = "country") %>%
  mutate(
    majority_pct       = sprintf("%.1f", majority_pct),
    minority_pct_total = sprintf("%.1f", minority_pct_total)
  ) %>%
  select(country, sample_size, majority_religion, majority_n, majority_pct,
         minority_n, minority_pct_total, minority_composition)

totals_row <- data_subset %>%
  filter(!is.na(religion_status)) %>%
  summarise(
    country              = "Total",
    sample_size          = n(),
    majority_religion    = "",
    majority_n           = sum(religion_status == "Majority"),
    majority_pct         = sprintf("%.1f", sum(religion_status == "Majority") / n() * 100),
    minority_n           = sum(religion_status == "Minority"),
    minority_pct_total   = sprintf("%.1f", sum(religion_status == "Minority") / n() * 100),
    minority_composition = ""
  )

table_subset <- bind_rows(table_subset, totals_row)

print(table_subset, n = nrow(table_subset))
```

Now we can filter the sample to only include countries that are in the
main analysis, and create Table 1 and save to a Word document.

```{r filter-sample}

# Drop countries with no majority
data <- data %>%
  filter(!country %in% countries_no_majority)

# Drop Macao SAR China
data <- data %>% filter(!country == "Macao SAR China") 

# Drop countries with <1% minority group
countries_drop <- country_check %>%
  filter(pct_minority < 1) %>%
  pull(country)

data <- data %>%
  filter(!country %in% countries_drop)

# Check remaining countries
data$country %>% unique() 
data$country %>% n_distinct() 

# Check final sample size
data %>% nrow()
```

## Check missingness

We need to check proportions of missingness for our three outcomes, and
whether religious minorities are more likely to not fill in outcome
data.

```{r check-missingness}

# Set WVS missing codes (-1, -2, -5) on life satisfaction to NA
data <- data %>% mutate(life_satisfaction = if_else(life_satisfaction < 0, NA_real_, life_satisfaction))

# Check missingness by religion status
data %>%
  filter(!is.na(religion_status)) %>%
  group_by(religion_status) %>%
  summarise(
    n = n(),
    
    miss_ls     = sum(is.na(life_satisfaction)),
    pct_ls      = round(mean(is.na(life_satisfaction)) * 100, 2),
    
    miss_happy  = sum(is.na(happiness)),
    pct_happy   = round(mean(is.na(happiness)) * 100, 2),
    
    miss_health = sum(is.na(health)),
    pct_health  = round(mean(is.na(health)) * 100, 2),
    
    miss_any    = sum(is.na(life_satisfaction) | is.na(happiness) | is.na(health)),
    pct_any     = round(mean(is.na(life_satisfaction) | is.na(happiness) | is.na(health)) * 100, 2)
  )

# Formally test whether minority status predicts missingness on any/each outcome
# Function to run missingness model for each outcome
run_missing_model <- function(missing_var, data) {
  cat("\n===== MISSINGNESS:", toupper(missing_var), "=====\n")
  
  fit <- glm(as.formula(paste(missing_var, "~ religion_status + age + sex")),
             data = data %>% filter(!is.na(religion_status)),
             family = binomial)
  
  results <- cbind(
    exp(cbind(OR = coef(fit), confint.default(fit))),
    p = summary(fit)$coefficients[, 4]
  ) %>%
    round(6)
  
  print(results)
}

# Create missingness indicators
data <- data %>%
  mutate(
    missing_ls     = as.numeric(is.na(life_satisfaction)),
    missing_happy  = as.numeric(is.na(happiness)),
    missing_health = as.numeric(is.na(health)),
    missing_any    = as.numeric(is.na(life_satisfaction) | is.na(happiness) | is.na(health))
  )

# Run for each outcome and overall
run_missing_model("missing_ls",     data)
run_missing_model("missing_happy",  data)
run_missing_model("missing_health", data)
run_missing_model("missing_any",    data)
```

It's good that we checked, because it appears religious minorities are
significantly less likely to complete questions on life satisfaction,
happiness, and general health.

This is an important point to raise in limitations.

In order to run our analytical models, we have to **remove those with
missing data on religious minority status (exposure), age & sex
(covariates), and all three outcomes** – so we keep individuals as long
as they have at least one of the three outcomes.

```{r remove-missing-outcome}

# Check N for each outcome individually
cat("N with valid life satisfaction:", sum(!is.na(data$life_satisfaction)), "\n")
cat("N with valid happiness:", sum(!is.na(data$happiness)), "\n")
cat("N with valid health:", sum(!is.na(data$health)), "\n")
cat("N missing on all three (to be excluded):",
    sum(is.na(data$life_satisfaction) & is.na(data$happiness) & is.na(data$health)), "\n")

# Apply filter - keep if valid on at least one outcome
data <- data %>%
  filter(!(is.na(life_satisfaction) & is.na(happiness) & is.na(health)))

summary(data$life_satisfaction)   # min should be 1

cat("\nFinal N after filter:", nrow(data), "\n")
cat("Countries:", n_distinct(data$country), "\n")
```

We now have 79,155 individuals who have at least one of three outcomes.

For analytical models with each of the outcomes, we have a different N:

- Life satisfaction - 78,803

- Happiness – 78,695

- General health – 79,005

# 3. DESCRIPTIVE SUMMARIES

## Descriptive statistics

Create descriptive statistics with the full sample. Majority is defined
as \>50% of population here.

```{r descriptive-stats}

data$religion_status %>% table()

# Descriptive statistics for key variables
vars_to_summarise <- c("life_satisfaction", "happiness", "health", 
                        "shi_matched", "gri_matched", "democracy_matched",
                        "gdp_matched", "gini_matched")

data %>%
  select(all_of(vars_to_summarise)) %>%
  pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = "variable", values_to = "value") %>%
  group_by(variable) %>%
  summarise(
    n        = sum(!is.na(value)),
    n_miss   = sum(is.na(value)),
    min      = round(min(value, na.rm = TRUE), 2),
    mean     = round(mean(value, na.rm = TRUE), 2),
    median   = round(median(value, na.rm = TRUE), 2),
    max      = round(max(value, na.rm = TRUE), 2),
    .groups  = "drop"
  ) %>%
  print(n = Inf)
```

Scales

- Life satisfaction: **1-10**

- Happiness: **1** (not at all happy) **- 4** (very happy) [re-coded in
  pre-processing]

- Subjective general health: **1** (very poor) **- 5** (very good)
  [re-coded in pre-processing]

- Government Restrictions Index (GRI): **0-10** [From Pew, matched to
  either year of collection or year before]

- Social Hostilities Index (SHI): **0-10** [From Pew, matched to either
  year of collection or year before]

- Democracy: **-10 - 10** [From Polity, matched to either year of
  collection or up to 5 years before]

- GDP: From World Bank, matched to either year of collection or year
  before

- Gini: **1-100** [From World Bank, matched to either year of collection
  or up to 5 years before]

- Religious freedom index: 0-10 [From WRD aggregated data, year not
  clear] (not included in analyses)

- Gender inequality: 0-1 [UNDP, 2018] (not included)

- Human Development Index: 0-1 [UNDP, 2018] (not included)

We have 79,152 individuals remaining – 56,395 majority, 22,757 minority.

# 4. CORRELATIONS

We will run correlations between outcomes and correlations between
indicators.

```{r outcome-correlations}
# Select variables
outcomes <- data %>% select(
  life_satisfaction, happiness, health
)

# Correlations 
outcomes %>% cor(use = "complete.obs")

# Correlation heat map
vis_cor(outcomes, cor_method = "pearson", cluster = FALSE)
```

```{r indicator-correlations}
# Select variables
variables <- data %>% select(
  gri_matched, shi_matched, democracy_matched, gdp_matched, gini_matched
)

# Correlations 
variables %>% cor(use = "complete.obs")

# Correlation heat map
vis_cor(variables, cor_method = "pearson", cluster = FALSE)
```

Observations:

\- Social hostilities and government restrictions moderately correlated
(0.50)

\- Democracy moderately negatively correlated with government
restrictions (-0.57) but not social hostilities (-0.12)

\- Government restrictions more strongly correlated to GDP and gini than
social restrictions

\- Religious freedom collinear - should not include

\- Gender inequality and human development collinear with GDP - should
not include

**Selection of macro-predictors: Social hostilities index, Government
restrictions index, GDP per capita, Gini index, Democracy index**

# 5. TWO-STAGE META-ANALYSIS

We will run two-stage meta-analyses for life satisfaction, happiness,
and general health separately.

For each outcome, we run linear regressions for each country, then pool
estimates into a random-effects meta-analysis.

For the first stage we use survey weights but multilevel models are
unweighted and adjusted for age and sex, with robust SEs.

## Life Satisfaction

For life satisfaction, first we run linear regressions for each country.

```{r linear-regressions-ls}
# Linear regressions for each country ----
country_models <- data %>% 
  nest(.by = country) %>% 
  mutate(models = lapply(data, function(df) 
    estimatr::lm_robust(life_satisfaction ~ religion_status + age + sex, data = df, weights = survey_weight, se_type = "HC2")))
country_models

country_estimates <- country_models %>% 
  mutate(tidy = lapply(models, broom::tidy)) %>% 
  unnest(tidy) %>% 
  filter(term == "religion_statusMinority") %>% 
  select(country, estimate, std.error)
country_estimates
```

Next, pool individual estimates into a meta-analysis for an overall
estimate across all countries.

```{r meta-analysis-ls}
# Random-effects meta-analysis ----
# With random-effects meta-analysis we can estimate cross-country heterogeneity in the gap, with I2 statistic. 

country_estimates <- country_estimates %>% arrange(estimate)
meta_model <- rma(
  yi = estimate,
  sei = std.error,
  data = country_estimates,
  method = "REML"
)

summary(meta_model)

predict(meta_model, digits = 3)
```

**Meta-analysis results**

I\^2: 81.3%, indicating substantial between-country heterogeneity.

Estimated minority-majority difference across countries: **-0.201** 95%
CI: **-0.297, -0.105**, p\<.0001

Q test significant: country effects more variable than expected by
chance

Prediction interval: -0.80 to +0.40 (true range of effects)

**Interpretations**

- There is substantial heterogeneity, differences are not explained by
  sampling error alone.

- Across countries, religious minorities score on average 0.20 points
  lower than majorities, on the 1-10 scale of life satisfaction.

**Plots**

We will include 3 plots for each analysis

- Forest plot - showing the gap between minority and majority

- Emmeans plot - showing the estimated marginal means for both majority
  and minority, to visualise the overall range of life satisfaction
  scores & gap for each country

- World map (Robinson's projection) - showing the variation in
  minority/majority gap between countries

***Forest plot***

```{r forest-plot-ls, echo=FALSE}
# Forest plot ----
forest_df <- country_estimates %>%
  mutate(
    ci.lb = estimate - 1.96 * std.error,
    ci.ub = estimate + 1.96 * std.error
  ) %>%
  arrange(estimate)
forest_df$` ` <- paste(rep(" ", 20), collapse = " ")
forest_df$ci_text <- sprintf("%.2f [%.2f, %.2f]", 
                              forest_df$estimate, 
                              forest_df$ci.lb, 
                              forest_df$ci.ub)
plot_df <- forest_df[, c("country", " ", "ci_text")]
colnames(plot_df) <- c("Country", " ", "Mean Difference [95% CI]")
w <- 1 / (forest_df$std.error^2)
psize <- sqrt(w)
psize <- psize / median(psize, na.rm = TRUE)
psize <- pmin(pmax(psize, 0.1), 0.5)
blank_row <- c("", paste(rep(" ", 20), collapse = " "), "")
plot_df_with_overall <- rbind(
  plot_df,
  blank_row,
  c("Overall", paste(rep(" ", 20), collapse = " "),
    sprintf("%.2f [%.2f, %.2f]", meta_model$beta, meta_model$ci.lb, meta_model$ci.ub)),
  blank_row
)
overall_est    <- c(forest_df$estimate, NA, as.numeric(meta_model$beta), NA)
overall_lower  <- c(forest_df$ci.lb,   NA, meta_model$ci.lb,            NA)
overall_upper  <- c(forest_df$ci.ub,   NA, meta_model$ci.ub,            NA)
overall_sizes  <- c(psize,             NA, 1,                            NA)
is_summary_vec <- c(rep(FALSE, nrow(plot_df) + 1), TRUE, FALSE)
overall_row <- nrow(plot_df_with_overall) - 1
p <- forest(
  data       = plot_df_with_overall[, c("Country", " ", "Mean Difference [95% CI]")],
  est        = overall_est,
  lower      = overall_lower,
  upper      = overall_upper,
  sizes      = overall_sizes,
  ci_column  = 2,
  ref_line   = 0,
  xlim       = c(-2, 2),
  ticks_at   = seq(-2, 2, 1),
  is_summary = is_summary_vec,
  row_height = unit(0.38, "cm"),
  theme = forest_theme(
    base_size    = 9,
    ci_lwd       = 1.2,
    ci_Theight   = 0.2,
    odd_row_col  = "#F0F0F0",
    even_row_col = "white",
    refline_gp   = gpar(lwd = 1, lty = "dashed", col = "black"),
    summary_fill = "black",
    summary_col  = "black",
    plot_margin  = unit(c(5, 5, 15, 5), "mm")  
  )
)
p <- insert_text(
  p,
  text = "Disparity in Life Satisfaction",
  row  = 1,
  col  = 1,
  part = "header",
  just = "left",
  gp   = gpar(fontsize = 12, fontface = "bold")
)
p <- add_border(p, 
                row  = nrow(plot_df),
                gp   = gpar(lwd = 1.0, col = "black"),
                part = "body")
p <- edit_plot(p, 
               row   = c(overall_row - 1, overall_row, overall_row + 1), 
               which = "background",
               gp    = gpar(fill = "#F0F0F0", col = NA))
p <- edit_plot(p, 
               row   = overall_row, 
               col   = 1,
               which = "text",
               gp    = gpar(fontface = "bold"))
p <- edit_plot(p,
               row   = overall_row,
               col   = 3,
               which = "text",
               gp    = gpar(fontface = "bold"))
ggsave("forest_life_satisfaction_gap.svg", plot = p, 
       width = 8, height = 13)

# Also view plot
print(p)
```

***Emmeans plot***

```{r emmeans-plot-ls, echo=FALSE}
# Plot minority/majority emmeans ----

## Country emmeans by group  
m_ls <- lm(life_satisfaction ~ religion_status * country + age + sex, data = data)

emmeans_ls <- emmeans(m_ls, ~ religion_status | country)

emmeans_df <- as.data.frame(emmeans_ls) %>% 
  select(country, religion_status, emmean, SE, lower.CL, upper.CL) %>% 
  rename(mean = emmean)

# Order countries by majority mean
order_df <- emmeans_df %>% 
  filter(religion_status == "Majority") %>% 
  arrange(mean) %>% 
  mutate(country_ordered = factor(country, levels = country))

emmeans_df <- emmeans_df %>% 
  left_join(order_df %>% select(country, country_ordered), by = "country")

# Plot minority and majority means

emmeans_p <- ggplot(emmeans_df,
       aes(x = mean,
           y = country_ordered,
           colour = religion_status,
           group = country)) +

  geom_line(linewidth = 0.6, alpha = 0.7) +
  geom_point(size = 2) +

  geom_errorbarh(
    aes(xmin = lower.CL, xmax = upper.CL),
    height = 0.30,
    alpha = 0.5
  ) +

  scale_colour_manual(
    values = c(
      "Majority" = "#04BFAF",
      "Minority" = "#0B2A5B"
    ),
    name = "Religious status"
  ) +

  scale_x_continuous(breaks = c(2,3,4,5,6,7,8,9)) +

  labs(
    x = "Mean life satisfaction",
    y = "Country",
    title = "Life satisfaction by religious minority/majority status within countries"
  ) +

  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "right")
ggsave("forest_life_satisfaction_gap_minmaj.svg", plot = emmeans_p, width = , height = 7)

# View plot
print(emmeans_p)
```

***World map projection***

```{r world-map-ls, echo=FALSE}
# World map ----
# Create country codes, not just country names 
country_estimates_map <- country_estimates %>%
  mutate(
    iso3c = countrycode(as.character(country), origin = "country.name", destination = "iso3c")
  )

# Plot size of gap on world map (Robinson's projection) - values from small to big 

# World polygons for mapping - use Robinson's projection for better visualisation of global patterns (equal area, less distortion of size)
world_sf <- ne_countries(scale = "medium", returnclass = "sf") %>%
  st_transform(crs = "+proj=robin")

# Join country estimates to world polygons
world_joined <- world_sf %>%
  left_join(country_estimates_map, by = c("iso_a3" = "iso3c"))

# Plot
p_map <- ggplot(world_joined) +
  geom_sf(aes(fill = estimate), color = "white", linewidth = 0.1) +
  coord_sf(crs = "+proj=robin") +
  scale_fill_gradient2(
    low = "#A40000",
    mid = "white",
    high = "#16317D",
    midpoint = 0,
    na.value = "grey90",
    limits = c(-1, 1),
    oob = scales::squish,
    name = "Gap (Minority - Majority)"
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Religious minority–majority gap in life satisfaction (by country)",
    caption = "Negative values indicate lower life satisfaction among religious minorities."
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    panel.grid = element_blank(),
    axis.text = element_blank(),
    axis.title = element_blank(),
    legend.position = "bottom",
    legend.justification = "center",
    plot.caption = element_text(size = 9, hjust = 0)
  )

p_map

ggsave("map_life_satisfaction_gap_robinson.svg", plot = p_map, width = 12, height = 6.8)
```

```{r emmeans-plot-health, echo=FALSE}
  geom_errorbarh(
    aes(xmin = lower.CL, xmax = upper.CL),
    height = 0.15,
    alpha = 0.5
  ) +

  scale_colour_manual(
    values = c(
      "Majority" = "#04BFAF",
      "Minority" = "#0B2A5B"
    ),
    name = "Religious status"
  ) +

  scale_x_continuous(breaks = c(2,3,4,5,6,7,8,9)) +

  labs(
    x = "Mean general health",
    y = "Country",
    title = "General health by religious minority/majority status within countries",
  ) +

  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "right",
        plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5))

       width = 6, height = 8)
```

# 6. SEX STRATIFICATION

Split by sex

```{r sex-split}
data_male   <- data %>% filter(sex == 1)
data_female <- data %>% filter(sex == 2)

cat("Men:", nrow(data_male), "| Women:", nrow(data_female),
    "| Total:", nrow(data_male) + nrow(data_female), "\n")
```

Sex-stratified two-stage meta-analyses

```{r sex-stratified-meta}
outcomes_all <- c("life_satisfaction", "happiness", "health")

sex_country_estimates <- function(dataset, sex_label) {
  map_dfr(outcomes_all, function(outcome) {
    dataset %>%
      nest(.by = country) %>%
      mutate(models = lapply(data, function(df)
        tryCatch(
          estimatr::lm_robust(as.formula(paste(outcome, "~ religion_status + age")),
                              data = df, weights = survey_weight, se_type = "HC2"),
          error = function(e) NULL))) %>%
      filter(!sapply(models, is.null)) %>%
      mutate(tidy = lapply(models, broom::tidy)) %>%
      unnest(tidy) %>%
      filter(term == "religion_statusMinority", !is.na(estimate)) %>%
      select(country, estimate, std.error) %>%
      mutate(outcome = outcome, sex_group = sex_label)
  })
}

sex_estimates <- bind_rows(
  sex_country_estimates(data_male,   "Male"),
  sex_country_estimates(data_female, "Female")
)

sex_meta <- sex_estimates %>%
  group_by(outcome, sex_group) %>%
  group_modify(~ {
    m <- rma(yi = estimate, sei = std.error, data = .x, method = "REML")
    tibble(estimate = m$b[1], ci_lb = m$ci.lb, ci_ub = m$ci.ub,
           p = m$pval, I2 = m$I2, k = m$k)
  }) %>%
  ungroup()

knitr::kable(sex_meta, digits = 3,
             caption = "Sex-stratified minority − majority gap (95% CI)")
```

Does the gap differ by sex? (two-stage interaction)

```{r sex-interaction-2s}
sex_interaction_2s <- map_dfr(outcomes_all, function(outcome) {
  data %>%
    nest(.by = country) %>%
    mutate(models = lapply(data, function(df)
      tryCatch(
        estimatr::lm_robust(as.formula(paste(outcome, "~ (religion_status + age) * factor(sex)")),
                            data = df, weights = survey_weight, se_type = "HC2"),
        error = function(e) NULL))) %>%
    filter(!sapply(models, is.null)) %>%
    mutate(tidy = lapply(models, broom::tidy)) %>%
    unnest(tidy) %>%
    filter(term == "religion_statusMinority:factor(sex)2", !is.na(estimate)) %>%
    select(country, estimate, std.error) %>%
    mutate(outcome = outcome)
})

sex_interaction_meta <- sex_interaction_2s %>%
  group_by(outcome) %>%
  group_modify(~ {
    m <- rma(yi = estimate, sei = std.error, data = .x, method = "REML", level = 90)
    tibble(estimate = m$b[1], ci_lb = m$ci.lb, ci_ub = m$ci.ub,
           p = m$pval, tau2 = m$tau2, I2 = m$I2, k = m$k)
  }) %>%
  ungroup()

knitr::kable(sex_interaction_meta, digits = 3,
             caption = "Sex difference in gap (women − men), 90% CI, α = 0.10")
```

# 7. MULTI-LEVEL MODELS - MODERATION ANALYSES

################################################################################ 

We have created estimates of the overall majority/minority gap in life
satisfaction, happiness, and general health.

Now, we will create multi-level models with individuals (Level 1) nested
within countries (Level 2), including random slopes and cross-level
interactions to test moderation effects of each country-level
macro-predictor.

The macro-predictors included are:

- government restrictions index

- Social hostilities index

- Democracy

- GDP per capita (log)

- Gini index.

For now we will not include religious minority group size, that will be
in a later section.

## Prepare country moderators for moderation analysis

We have to create a country macro-predictors dataset, by country rather
than individual.

```{r macro-predictors-dataset}
# Create country macro-predictors dataset
country_data <- data %>% 
  group_by(country) %>% 
  summarise(
    gri_matched = first(gri_matched),
    shi_matched = first(shi_matched),
    democracy_matched = first(democracy_matched),
    gdp_matched = first(gdp_matched),
    gini_matched = first(gini_matched)
  )
```

Next, we will standardise macro-predictors in case needed for future
analyses.

We log transform GDP as per protocol. We also mean centre it
subsequently to reduce skew and better capture relative differences
between countries. For others, we also z score in case of use in the
future.

```{r transformation-moderators}
# Z Score variables & log transform/mean centre GDP
country_data <- country_data %>%
  mutate(
    gri_z = as.numeric(scale(gri_matched)),
    shi_z = as.numeric(scale(shi_matched)),
    democracy_z = as.numeric(scale(democracy_matched)),
    log_gdp = log(gdp_matched), # log transform
    log_gdp_c = log_gdp - mean(log_gdp, na.rm = TRUE), # then mean centre 
    gini_z = as.numeric(scale(gini_matched))
  )

# Merge back to individual dataset 
data <- data %>% 
  left_join(country_data %>% select(country, gri_z, shi_z, democracy_z, log_gdp, log_gdp_c, gini_z), by = "country")
```

For GRI and SHI, we can treat them as continuous numerical measures.
However, Pew Research Center also creates categories with SHI, including
low, moderate, high, and very high. Following Pew instructions
(<https://www.pewresearch.org/religion/2024/03/05/restrictions-methodology/>),
we will run models with categorical variables and plot with thresholds.

## Create pipeline & run all country predictor moderation models

We want to run a series of models for our three outcomes: life
satisfaction, happiness, and general health. To simplify the process,
rather than copy and pasting the code three times we can just create a
pipeline to repeat the same models for each of the outcome, and save
respective plots.

Here are the models we need to run for each outcome:

1.  Null model (with only random intercepts to calculate VPC)

2.  Unadjusted model (with only religion status as predictor)

3.  Adjusted model (with covariates)

4.  Random slope (allowing minority/majority gap to vary across
    countries)

5.  Log likelihood test (to compare random slope vs random intercept
    model)

6.  GRI continuous

7.  GRI categorical

8.  SHI continuous

9.  SHI categorical

10. Democracy index continuous

11. GDP per capita continuous

12. Gini index continuous

```{r outcome-pipline}
run_outcome_pipeline <- function(outcome_var, input_data) {
  
  df <- input_data
  
  # Print clear header so output is easy to navigate
  cat("\n")
  cat("========================================\n")
  cat("  OUTCOME:", toupper(gsub("_", " ", outcome_var)), "\n")
  cat("========================================\n")
  
  f <- function(rhs) as.formula(paste(outcome_var, "~", rhs))
  
  # Create all derived variables inside function so it's self-contained
  df <- df %>%
    mutate(
      # log GDP if not already present
      log_gdp = if ("log_gdp" %in% names(df)) log_gdp else log(gdp_matched),
      # GRI categories
      gri_category = case_when(
        gri_matched >= 6.6 ~ "Very High",
        gri_matched >= 4.5 ~ "High",
        gri_matched >= 2.4 ~ "Moderate",
        gri_matched >= 0.0 ~ "Low"
      ),
      gri_category = factor(gri_category, levels = c("Low", "Moderate", "High", "Very High")),
      # SHI categories
      shi_category = case_when(
        shi_matched >= 7.2 ~ "Very High",
        shi_matched >= 3.6 ~ "High",
        shi_matched >= 1.5 ~ "Moderate",
        shi_matched >= 0.0 ~ "Low"
      ),
      shi_category = factor(shi_category, levels = c("Low", "Moderate", "High", "Very High"))
    )
  
  # 1. Null model
  cat("\n===== NULL MODEL =====\n")
  null_mod <- lmer(f("1 + (1 | country)"), data = df, REML = FALSE)
  print(summary(null_mod))
  vc <- as.data.frame(VarCorr(null_mod))
  var_country <- vc$vcov[vc$grp == "country" & vc$var1 == "(Intercept)"]
  var_resid <- attr(VarCorr(null_mod), "sc")^2
  VPC <- var_country / (var_country + var_resid)
  cat("VPC:", VPC, "(", VPC * 100, "%)\n")
  
  # 2. Unadjusted
  cat("\n===== UNADJUSTED MODEL =====\n")
  ls_unadj <- lmer(f("religion_status + (1 | country)"), data = df, REML = FALSE)
  print(summary(ls_unadj))
  print(confint(ls_unadj, method = "Wald"))
  
  # 3. Adjusted
  cat("\n===== ADJUSTED MODEL =====\n")
  ls_adj <- lmer(f("religion_status + age + sex + (1 | country)"), data = df, REML = FALSE)
  print(summary(ls_adj))
  print(confint(ls_adj, method = "Wald"))
  
  # 4. Random slope
  cat("\n===== RANDOM SLOPE MODEL =====\n")
  ls_slope <- lmer(f("religion_status + age + sex + (1 + religion_status | country)"),
                   data = df, REML = FALSE,
                   control = lmerControl(optimizer = "bobyqa"))
  print(summary(ls_slope))
  print(confint(ls_slope, method = "Wald"))
  
  # 5. Log likelihood test - use df_ll not df to avoid overwriting the dataframe
  cat("\n===== LOG LIKELIHOOD TEST =====\n")
  LR    <- 2 * (as.numeric(logLik(ls_slope)) - as.numeric(logLik(ls_adj)))
  df_ll <- attr(logLik(ls_slope), "df") - attr(logLik(ls_adj), "df")
  p     <- pchisq(LR, df = df_ll, lower.tail = FALSE)
  cat("LR:", LR, "df:", df_ll, "p:", p, "\n")
  
  # Helper: continuous predictor plot
  plot_continuous <- function(fit, predictor, x_label, df) {
    at_list <- list(seq(min(df[[predictor]], na.rm = TRUE),
                        max(df[[predictor]], na.rm = TRUE),
                        length.out = 20))
    names(at_list) <- predictor
    
    emm_levels <- emmeans(fit,
                          as.formula(paste("~ religion_status |", predictor)),
                          at = at_list)
    emm_df <- as.data.frame(emm_levels) %>%
      mutate(religion_status = as.character(religion_status))
    emm_df_slim <- emm_df %>% select(religion_status, all_of(predictor), emmean)
    
    country_means <- df %>%  # df not data
      group_by(country, religion_status) %>%
      summarise(
        mean_out = mean(.data[[outcome_var]], na.rm = TRUE),
        pred_val = mean(.data[[predictor]], na.rm = TRUE),
        n = n(),
        .groups = "drop"
      ) %>%
      mutate(
        pred_snapped = as.numeric(sapply(pred_val, function(d) {
          emm_df_slim[[predictor]][which.min(abs(emm_df_slim[[predictor]] - d))]
        }))
      ) %>%
      rename(!!predictor := pred_snapped) %>%
      left_join(emm_df_slim, by = c("religion_status", predictor)) 
    
    p <- ggplot(emm_df, aes(x = .data[[predictor]], y = emmean, color = religion_status)) +
      geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
      geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = asymp.LCL, ymax = asymp.UCL, fill = religion_status),
                  alpha = 0.2, color = NA) +
      geom_point(data = country_means,
                 aes(x = pred_val, y = mean_out, size = n, color = religion_status),
                 alpha = 0.6) +
      scale_size_continuous(name = "Sample size", range = c(2, 10)) +
      scale_color_manual(values = c("Majority" = "#04BFAF", "Minority" = "#0B2A5B")) +
      labs(x = x_label, 
           y = paste("Mean", gsub("_", " ", outcome_var)),
           title = paste(tools::toTitleCase(gsub("_", " ", outcome_var)), "by minority/majority status across", x_label),
           color = "Religion status", fill = "Religion status") +
      theme_minimal() +
      theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5))
    
    ggsave(paste0("emmeans_", predictor, "_", outcome_var, ".svg"), plot = p, width = 12, height = 5.8)
    print(p)
  }
  
  # Helper: categorical predictor plot
  plot_categorical <- function(fit, predictor, x_label, df) {
    emm_cat <- emmeans(fit, as.formula(paste("~ religion_status |", predictor)))
    emm_df_cat <- as.data.frame(emm_cat) %>%
      mutate(religion_status = as.character(religion_status))
    
    country_means <- df %>%  # df not data
      filter(!is.na(.data[[predictor]])) %>%
      group_by(country, religion_status, .data[[predictor]]) %>%
      summarise(mean_out = mean(.data[[outcome_var]], na.rm = TRUE), n = n(), .groups = "drop") %>%
      left_join(emm_df_cat %>% select(religion_status, all_of(predictor), emmean),
                by = c("religion_status", predictor)) 

    
    p <- ggplot(emm_df_cat, aes(x = .data[[predictor]], y = emmean,
                                color = religion_status, group = religion_status)) +
      geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
      geom_point(size = 3) +
      geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = asymp.LCL, ymax = asymp.UCL), width = 0.2) +
      geom_point(data = country_means,
                 aes(x = .data[[predictor]], y = mean_out, size = n, color = religion_status),
                 alpha = 0.4,
                 position = position_jitterdodge(jitter.width = 0.05, dodge.width = 0.3)) +
      scale_size_continuous(name = "Sample size", range = c(1, 7)) +
      scale_color_manual(values = c("Majority" = "#04BFAF", "Minority" = "#0B2A5B")) +
      scale_fill_manual(values = c("Majority" = "#04BFAF", "Minority" = "#0B2A5B"),
                  name = "Religion status") +
      labs(x = x_label, y = paste("Mean", gsub("_", " ", outcome_var)),
           title = paste(tools::toTitleCase(gsub("_", " ", outcome_var)), "by religious status across", x_label),
           color = "Religion status") +
      theme_minimal() +
      theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5))
    
    ggsave(paste0("emmeans_", predictor, "_", outcome_var, ".svg"), plot = p, width = 12, height = 5.8)
    print(p)
    
    gaps <- pairs(emm_cat, reverse = TRUE)   # reuse emm_cat; Minority − Majority
    
    cat("\n--- Simple effects (unadjusted) ---\n")
    print(summary(gaps, infer = c(TRUE, TRUE)))
    
    cat("\n--- Simple effects (adjusted across", nlevels(df[[predictor]]), "categories) ---\n")
    gaps_adj <- summary(gaps, by = NULL, adjust = "mvt", infer = c(TRUE, TRUE))
    print(gaps_adj)
    
    invisible(gaps_adj)
  }
  
  # 6. GRI continuous
  cat("\n===== GRI CONTINUOUS =====\n")
  fit_gri <- lmer(f("religion_status * gri_matched + age + sex + (1 + religion_status | country)"),
                  data = df, REML = FALSE)
  print(summary(fit_gri)); print(confint(fit_gri, method = "Wald", level = 0.90))
  plot_continuous(fit_gri, "gri_matched", "Government Restrictions Index (GRI)", df)
  
  # 7. GRI categorical
  cat("\n===== GRI CATEGORICAL =====\n")
  fit_gri_cat <- lmer(f("religion_status * gri_category + age + sex + (1 + religion_status | country)"),
                      data = df, REML = FALSE)
  print(summary(fit_gri_cat)); print(confint(fit_gri_cat, method = "Wald", level = 0.90))
  gri_simple <- plot_categorical(fit_gri_cat, "gri_category", "Government Restrictions Index (GRI)", df)
  
  # 8. SHI continuous
  cat("\n===== SHI CONTINUOUS =====\n")
  fit_shi <- lmer(f("religion_status * shi_matched + age + sex + (1 + religion_status | country)"),
                  data = df, REML = FALSE)
  print(summary(fit_shi)); print(confint(fit_shi, method = "Wald", level = 0.90))
  plot_continuous(fit_shi, "shi_matched", "Social Hostilities Index (SHI)", df)
  
  # 9. SHI categorical
  cat("\n===== SHI CATEGORICAL =====\n")
  fit_shi_cat <- lmer(f("religion_status * shi_category + age + sex + (1 + religion_status | country)"),
                      data = df, REML = FALSE)
  print(summary(fit_shi_cat)); print(confint(fit_shi_cat, method = "Wald", level = 0.90))
  shi_simple <- plot_categorical(fit_shi_cat, "shi_category", "Social Hostilities Index (SHI)", df)
  
  # 10. Democracy
  cat("\n===== DEMOCRACY =====\n")
  fit_dem <- lmer(f("religion_status * democracy_matched + age + sex + (1 + religion_status | country)"),
                  data = df, REML = FALSE)
  print(summary(fit_dem)); print(confint(fit_dem, method = "Wald", level = 0.90))
  plot_continuous(fit_dem, "democracy_matched", "Democracy Index", df)
  
  # 11. GDP
  cat("\n===== GDP =====\n")
  fit_gdp <- lmer(f("religion_status * log_gdp + age + sex + (1 + religion_status | country)"),
                  data = df, REML = FALSE)
  print(summary(fit_gdp)); print(confint(fit_gdp, method = "Wald", level = 0.90))
  plot_continuous(fit_gdp, "log_gdp", "Log GDP per capita", df)
  
  # 12. Gini
  cat("\n===== GINI =====\n")
  fit_gini <- lmer(f("religion_status * gini_matched + age + sex + (1 + religion_status | country)"),
                   data = df, REML = FALSE)
  print(summary(fit_gini)); print(confint(fit_gini, method = "Wald", level = 0.90))
  plot_continuous(fit_gini, "gini_matched", "Gini Index", df)
  
  invisible(list(
    null = null_mod, unadj = ls_unadj, adj = ls_adj, slope = ls_slope,
    gri = fit_gri, gri_cat = fit_gri_cat, gri_simple = gri_simple,
    shi = fit_shi, shi_cat = fit_shi_cat, shi_simple = shi_simple,
    democracy = fit_dem, gdp = fit_gdp, gini = fit_gini
  ))
}

set.seed(2026)
results_ls     <- run_outcome_pipeline("life_satisfaction", data)
results_happy  <- run_outcome_pipeline("happiness", data)
results_health <- run_outcome_pipeline("health", data)

get_interactions <- function(res, outcome) {
  map_dfr(c("gri", "gri_cat", "shi", "shi_cat", "democracy", "gdp", "gini"), function(m) {
    tidy(res[[m]], effects = "fixed", conf.int = TRUE,
         conf.level = 0.90, conf.method = "Wald") %>%
      filter(grepl(":", term)) %>%
      mutate(model = m, outcome = outcome)
  })
}

interactions <- bind_rows(
  get_interactions(results_ls,     "life_satisfaction"),
  get_interactions(results_happy,  "happiness"),
  get_interactions(results_health, "health")
)

simple_effects <- bind_rows(
  as.data.frame(results_ls$gri_simple)     %>% mutate(outcome = "life_satisfaction", index = "GRI"),
  as.data.frame(results_ls$shi_simple)     %>% mutate(outcome = "life_satisfaction", index = "SHI"),
  as.data.frame(results_happy$gri_simple)  %>% mutate(outcome = "happiness",         index = "GRI"),
  as.data.frame(results_happy$shi_simple)  %>% mutate(outcome = "happiness",         index = "SHI"),
  as.data.frame(results_health$gri_simple) %>% mutate(outcome = "health",            index = "GRI"),
  as.data.frame(results_health$shi_simple) %>% mutate(outcome = "health",            index = "SHI")
)

interactions %>%
  mutate(term = gsub("religion_statusMinority:", "", term),
         clear = if_else(p.value < 0.10, "yes", "no")) %>%
  select(outcome, model, term, estimate, conf.low, conf.high, p.value, clear) %>%
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ round(.x, 3))) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = "Interaction terms for all country-level indicators (90% Wald CIs, α = 0.10)")

simple_effects %>%
  mutate(category = coalesce(as.character(gri_category), as.character(shi_category))) %>%
  select(outcome, index, category, estimate,
         lower.CL = any_of(c("asymp.LCL", "lower.CL")),
         upper.CL = any_of(c("asymp.UCL", "upper.CL")), p.value) %>%
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ round(.x, 3))) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = "Simple effects: minority − majority gap (mvt-adjusted 95% CIs)")
```

### Multi-panel figure for Supplementary files

```{r supp-moderation-panels, fig.width=14, fig.height=9}
library(patchwork)
emm_options(lmer.df = "asymptotic")   # same asymptotic CIs as the pipeline, without the d.f. notes

# Recreate the derived variables used in the pipeline
df_supp <- data %>%
  mutate(
    log_gdp = if ("log_gdp" %in% names(data)) log_gdp else log(gdp_matched),
    gri_category = factor(case_when(
      gri_matched >= 6.6 ~ "Very High", gri_matched >= 4.5 ~ "High",
      gri_matched >= 2.4 ~ "Moderate",  gri_matched >= 0.0 ~ "Low"
    ), levels = c("Low", "Moderate", "High", "Very High")),
    shi_category = factor(case_when(
      shi_matched >= 7.2 ~ "Very High", shi_matched >= 3.6 ~ "High",
      shi_matched >= 1.5 ~ "Moderate",  shi_matched >= 0.0 ~ "Low"
    ), levels = c("Low", "Moderate", "High", "Very High"))
  )

# Shared scales so the legends merge across panels
group_cols <- c("Majority" = "#04BFAF", "Minority" = "#0B2A5B")
max_n <- df_supp %>% count(country, religion_status) %>% pull(n) %>% max()
size_scale <- scale_size_continuous(name = "Country sample size", range = c(0.8, 5),
                                    limits = c(1, max_n))

# Categorical panel (GRI, SHI)
panel_cat <- function(fit, predictor, x_label, outcome_var, y_label) {
  emm_df <- as.data.frame(emmeans(fit, as.formula(paste("~ religion_status |", predictor)))) %>%
    rename(any_of(c(lower.CL = "asymp.LCL", upper.CL = "asymp.UCL"))) %>%
    mutate(religion_status = as.character(religion_status))
  
  country_means <- df_supp %>%
    filter(!is.na(.data[[predictor]]), !is.na(.data[[outcome_var]])) %>%
    group_by(country, religion_status, .data[[predictor]]) %>%
    summarise(mean_out = mean(.data[[outcome_var]]), n = n(), .groups = "drop")
  
  ggplot(emm_df, aes(x = .data[[predictor]], y = emmean,
                     colour = religion_status, group = religion_status)) +
    geom_point(data = country_means,
               aes(x = .data[[predictor]], y = mean_out, size = n, colour = religion_status),
               alpha = 0.25, inherit.aes = FALSE,
               position = position_jitterdodge(jitter.width = 0.05, dodge.width = 0.3, seed = 2026)) +
    geom_line(linewidth = 0.9) +
    geom_point(size = 2.5) +
    geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = lower.CL, ymax = upper.CL), width = 0.15) +
    scale_colour_manual(values = group_cols, name = "Religious status") +
    size_scale +
    labs(x = x_label, y = y_label) +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
    theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank())
}

# Continuous panel (democracy, GDP, Gini)
panel_cont <- function(fit, predictor, x_label, outcome_var, y_label) {
  rng <- range(df_supp[[predictor]], na.rm = TRUE)
  at_list <- setNames(list(seq(rng[1], rng[2], length.out = 30)), predictor)
  
  emm_df <- as.data.frame(emmeans(fit, as.formula(paste("~ religion_status |", predictor)),
                                  at = at_list)) %>%
    rename(any_of(c(lower.CL = "asymp.LCL", upper.CL = "asymp.UCL"))) %>%
    mutate(religion_status = as.character(religion_status))
  
  country_means <- df_supp %>%
    filter(!is.na(.data[[predictor]]), !is.na(.data[[outcome_var]])) %>%
    group_by(country, religion_status) %>%
    summarise(mean_out = mean(.data[[outcome_var]]),
              pred_val = mean(.data[[predictor]]), n = n(), .groups = "drop")
  
  ggplot(emm_df, aes(x = .data[[predictor]], y = emmean, colour = religion_status)) +
    geom_point(data = country_means,
               aes(x = pred_val, y = mean_out, size = n, colour = religion_status),
               alpha = 0.25, inherit.aes = FALSE) +
    geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = lower.CL, ymax = upper.CL, fill = religion_status),
                alpha = 0.2, colour = NA, show.legend = FALSE) +
    geom_line(linewidth = 0.9) +
    scale_colour_manual(values = group_cols, name = "Religious status") +
    scale_fill_manual(values = group_cols, guide = "none") +
    size_scale +
    labs(x = x_label, y = y_label) +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
    theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank())
}

# One five-panel figure per outcome
make_supp_figure <- function(res, outcome_var, outcome_label, file_name) {
  y_lab <- paste("Mean", outcome_label)
  
  pA <- panel_cat(res$gri_cat, "gri_category", "Government Restrictions Index", outcome_var, y_lab)
  pB <- panel_cat(res$shi_cat, "shi_category", "Social Hostilities Index",      outcome_var, y_lab)
  pC <- panel_cont(res$democracy, "democracy_matched", "Democracy index (Polity)", outcome_var, y_lab)
  pD <- panel_cont(res$gdp,       "log_gdp",           "Log GDP per capita",       outcome_var, y_lab)
  pE <- panel_cont(res$gini,      "gini_matched",      "Gini index",               outcome_var, y_lab)
  
  fig <- (pA | pB | pC) / (pD | pE | guide_area()) +
    plot_layout(guides = "collect") +
    plot_annotation(
      title = paste(tools::toTitleCase(outcome_label),
                    "among religious minorities and majorities by country-level indicators"),
      tag_levels = "A",
      caption = paste("Lines, points and error bars/bands: estimated marginal means (95% CI) from multilevel models",
                      "with religious status × indicator interactions, adjusted for age and sex.",
                      "\nCircles: observed country-level means for majority and minority groups, sized by sample size.")
    ) &
    theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, size = 13),
          plot.caption = element_text(hjust = 0, size = 8, colour = "grey40"))
  
  ggsave(file_name, plot = fig, width = 14, height = 9)
  fig
}

fig_supp_ls     <- make_supp_figure(results_ls,     "life_satisfaction", "life satisfaction", "supp_moderation_life_satisfaction.svg")
fig_supp_happy  <- make_supp_figure(results_happy,  "happiness",         "happiness",         "supp_moderation_happiness.svg")
fig_supp_health <- make_supp_figure(results_health, "health",            "general health",    "supp_moderation_health.svg")

fig_supp_ls
fig_supp_happy
fig_supp_health
```

### Create Figure 4 in results

For the manuscript we will only present GRI and SHI moderation for life
satisfaction.

```{r figure4, fig.width=6.5, fig.height=8}
outcome_var <- "life_satisfaction"

df <- data %>%
  mutate(
    gri_category = factor(case_when(
      gri_matched >= 6.6 ~ "Very High",
      gri_matched >= 4.5 ~ "High",

    ), levels = c("Low", "Moderate", "High", "Very High"))
  )

panel_categorical <- function(predictor, x_label) {
  fit <- lmer(as.formula(paste0(
    outcome_var, " ~ religion_status * ", predictor,
    " + age + sex + (1 + religion_status | country)")),
    data = df, REML = FALSE,

  cat("\n===== ", toupper(predictor), " =====\n", sep = "")
  print(summary(pairs(emm, reverse = TRUE), infer = c(TRUE, TRUE)))
  
  ggplot(emm_df, aes(x = .data[[predictor]], y = emmean,

                                  "Minority" = "#0B2A5B"),
                       name = "Religion status") +
    labs(x = x_label, y = "Mean life satisfaction") +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 11)
}
```

## Run religious minority group size moderation models

After running the moderation analyses for country-level indices, we can
now test the moderation effect of size of religious minority groups on
the minority/majority gap.

The question we ask is essentially, would a very small minority group
(e.g. 2%) within a country generally fare better/worse than a medium
minority group (e.g. 30%)?

To test this, we need to extract the exact % of each minority group
within their respective country according to the **World Religion
Database** (not the actual sample size in WVS as it may not be
representative). We have previously created demographic tables and need
to call them from Pre-processing.R file. We can then run a model to see
whether the proportion of population of each minority group within each
country affects the minority/majority gap.

```{r check-minority-sizes}
n_before <- nrow(data)

data_size <- data %>%
  left_join(wrd_long, by = c("country", "religion_wrd" = "religion")) %>%
  rename(pct_own_group = wrd_share)

stopifnot(nrow(data_size) == n_before)   # errors if the join duplicated rows

# Minorities above 50% (should be none or explainable)
data_size %>%
  filter(religion_status == "Minority", pct_own_group > 50) %>%
  distinct(country, religion_wrd, pct_own_group)

# Smallest groups
data_size %>%
  filter(religion_status == "Minority") %>%
  distinct(country, religion_wrd, pct_own_group) %>%
  arrange(pct_own_group) %>%
  head(20)

```

```{r moderation-minority-group-size}
# min_size_c for interaction term minority x size 

data_size <- data_size %>%
  mutate(min_size_c = if_else(religion_status == "Minority", pct_own_group - 10, 0))

data_size %>%
  filter(religion_status == "Minority") %>%
  summarise(min = min(pct_own_group, na.rm = TRUE),
            median = median(pct_own_group, na.rm = TRUE),
            max = max(pct_own_group, na.rm = TRUE),
            n_missing = sum(is.na(pct_own_group)))

run_minsize <- function(outcome_var) {
  cat("\n===== MINORITY GROUP SIZE:", toupper(gsub("_", " ", outcome_var)), "=====\n")
  fit <- lmer(
    as.formula(paste(outcome_var,
                     "~ religion_status + min_size_c + age + sex + (1 + religion_status | country)")),
    data = data_size, REML = FALSE,
    control = lmerControl(optimizer = "bobyqa")
  )
  print(summary(fit))
  ci <- confint(fit, method = "Wald", level = 0.90)
  print(ci)
  
  b <- fixef(fit)["min_size_c"]
  cat("\nChange in gap per 10 pp larger minority:",
      round(10 * b, 3), "[90% CI", round(10 * ci["min_size_c", 1], 3), ",",
      round(10 * ci["min_size_c", 2], 3), "]\n")
  fit
}

fit_minsize_ls     <- run_minsize("life_satisfaction")
fit_minsize_happy  <- run_minsize("happiness")
fit_minsize_health <- run_minsize("health")
```

Here are the summary of results on religious minority group size from
moderation models.

Life satisfaction

- Interaction was significant (β = 0.005, p = .07)

- In sensitivity analysis (excluding \>50%) also significant (β = 0.006,
  p = .07)

Happiness

- Interaction non-significant in both the full (β = 0.001, p = .241) and
  sensitivity (β = 0.001, p = .542) samples

- Group size did not moderate

General health

- Full sample the interaction was significant (β = 0.003, p = .014) —
  smaller minority group size, larger minority–majority health gap

- But this effect disappeared when excluding \>50% groups (β = 0.002, p
  = .176), suggesting the moderation effect was largely driven by the
  over-represented minority groups (mostly No Denomination in secular
  countries) rather than reflecting a genuine minority group size effect

**Overall conclusion:**

Minority group size moderates the minority–majority life satisfaction
gap across outcomes but the estimate is very small - less than 0.01
points on a 1-10 scale. The general health finding was not replicated
when excluding countries where 'minorities' were actually \>50% of the
sample.

```{r plot-minority-group-size, fig.width=12, fig.height=4.8}
library(patchwork)

# Common size scale across panels so the legends merge
max_n <- data_size %>%
  filter(religion_status == "Minority") %>%
  count(country, religion_wrd) %>%
  pull(n) %>% max()

plot_gap_size <- function(fit, outcome_var, y_label) {
  # Model-implied gap and 90% CI across observed minority sizes
  rng   <- range(data_size$pct_own_group[data_size$religion_status == "Minority"], na.rm = TRUE)
  sizes <- seq(rng[1], rng[2], length.out = 50)
  idx   <- c("religion_statusMinority", "min_size_c")
  L     <- cbind(1, sizes - 10)
  est   <- as.vector(L %*% fixef(fit)[idx])
  se    <- sqrt(rowSums((L %*% as.matrix(vcov(fit)[idx, idx])) * L))
  z     <- qnorm(0.95)   # 90% CI
  line_df <- tibble(size = sizes, gap = est,
                    lower = est - z * se, upper = est + z * se)
  
  # Observed (unadjusted) gap for each minority group vs its country's majority
  maj_means <- data_size %>%
    filter(religion_status == "Majority") %>%
    group_by(country) %>%
    summarise(maj_mean = mean(.data[[outcome_var]], na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")
  
  group_gaps <- data_size %>%
    filter(religion_status == "Minority") %>%
    group_by(country, religion_wrd) %>%
    summarise(size = first(pct_own_group),
              min_mean = mean(.data[[outcome_var]], na.rm = TRUE),
              n = sum(!is.na(.data[[outcome_var]])), .groups = "drop") %>%
    left_join(maj_means, by = "country") %>%
    mutate(gap = min_mean - maj_mean)
  
  ggplot() +
    geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey50") +
    geom_point(data = group_gaps, aes(x = size, y = gap, size = n),
               colour = "#0B2A5B", alpha = 0.35) +
    geom_ribbon(data = line_df, aes(x = size, ymin = lower, ymax = upper),
                fill = "#04BFAF", alpha = 0.3) +
    geom_line(data = line_df, aes(x = size, y = gap),
              colour = "#04BFAF", linewidth = 1) +
    scale_size_continuous(name = "Minority group n", range = c(1, 6),
                          limits = c(1, max_n)) +
    labs(x = "Minority group size (% of national population)",
         y = paste("Minority – majority gap in\n", y_label)) +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
    theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank())
}

p_ls     <- plot_gap_size(fit_minsize_ls,     "life_satisfaction", "life satisfaction")
p_happy  <- plot_gap_size(fit_minsize_happy,  "happiness",         "happiness")
p_health <- plot_gap_size(fit_minsize_health, "health",            "general health")

combined_size <- (p_ls | p_happy | p_health) +
  plot_layout(guides = "collect", axis_titles = "collect") +
  plot_annotation(
    tag_levels = "A",
    caption = "Line and band: model-estimated gap (adjusted for age and sex) with 90% CI. Points: unadjusted gap for each minority group vs its country's majority. Group size from World Religion Database 2020."
  ) &
  theme(legend.position = "right",
        plot.caption = element_text(hjust = 0, size = 8, colour = "grey40"))

ggsave("gap_by_minority_size_combined.svg", plot = combined_size,
       width = 12, height = 4.8)
print(combined_size)
```

```{r save-dashboard-outputs}
# ---- Pooled meta-analysis results ----
meta_summary <- map_dfr(
  list(life_satisfaction = meta_model,
       happiness         = meta_model_hap,
       health            = meta_model_gh),
  function(m) {
    pr <- predict(m)
    tibble(estimate = as.numeric(m$b), se = m$se,
           ci_lb = m$ci.lb, ci_ub = m$ci.ub, p = m$pval,
           pi_lb = pr$pi.lb, pi_ub = pr$pi.ub,
           I2 = m$I2, tau2 = m$tau2, k = m$k)
  },
  .id = "outcome"
)

# ---- VPC from null models ----
get_vpc <- function(fit) {
  vc <- as.data.frame(VarCorr(fit))
  v_country <- vc$vcov[vc$grp == "country"]
  v_resid   <- vc$vcov[vc$grp == "Residual"]
  v_country / (v_country + v_resid)
}
vpc <- tibble(
  outcome = c("life_satisfaction", "happiness", "health"),
  vpc     = c(get_vpc(results_ls$null), get_vpc(results_happy$null), get_vpc(results_health$null))
)

# ---- Country-level indicators with Pew categories ----
country_indicators <- country_data %>%
  mutate(
    gri_category = factor(case_when(
      gri_matched >= 6.6 ~ "Very High", gri_matched >= 4.5 ~ "High",
      gri_matched >= 2.4 ~ "Moderate",  gri_matched >= 0.0 ~ "Low"
    ), levels = c("Low", "Moderate", "High", "Very High")),
    shi_category = factor(case_when(
      shi_matched >= 7.2 ~ "Very High", shi_matched >= 3.6 ~ "High",
      shi_matched >= 1.5 ~ "Moderate",  shi_matched >= 0.0 ~ "Low"
    ), levels = c("Low", "Moderate", "High", "Very High"))
  ) %>%
  select(country, gri_matched, shi_matched, democracy_matched,
         gdp_matched, gini_matched, gri_category, shi_category)

# ---- Moderation: simple effects (gap within each GRI/SHI category) ----
simple_effects_clean <- simple_effects %>%
  rename(any_of(c(lower.CL = "asymp.LCL", upper.CL = "asymp.UCL"))) %>%
  mutate(category = coalesce(as.character(gri_category), as.character(shi_category)),
         category = factor(category, levels = c("Low", "Moderate", "High", "Very High"))) %>%
  transmute(outcome, index, category, estimate, se = SE,
            ci_lb = lower.CL, ci_ub = upper.CL, p = p.value)

# ---- Moderation: interaction terms (90% CIs, alpha = 0.10) ----
interactions_clean <- interactions %>%
  transmute(outcome, model,
            term = gsub("religion_statusMinority:", "", term),
            estimate, se = std.error,
            ci_lb = conf.low, ci_ub = conf.high, p = p.value)

# ---- Bundle and save ----
model_outputs <- list(
  country_estimates = bind_rows(
    country_estimates     %>% mutate(outcome = "life_satisfaction"),
    country_estimates_hap %>% mutate(outcome = "happiness"),
    country_estimates_gh  %>% mutate(outcome = "health"),
  ),
  meta_summary       = meta_summary,
  vpc                = vpc,
  country_indicators = country_indicators,
  simple_effects     = simple_effects_clean,
  interactions       = interactions_clean,
  sex_country_estimates = sex_estimates,
  sex_meta              = sex_meta,
  sex_interaction_meta  = sex_interaction_meta,
  saved_on           = Sys.Date()
)

saveRDS(model_outputs, "dashboard_model_outputs.rds")
```
